profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer | Node.js • Distributed Systems • DX Architect
profile.summary: I am a Senior Software Engineer with 14 years of experience building stable, high-performance web systems. My career has focused on taking fragmented legacy environments and moving them toward modern standards like Edge computing and native Web APIs. I prioritize developer experience and system resilience because I believe the best tools are the ones that stay out of the developer's way. Whether I am architecting runtime-agnostic proxies or migrating monoliths to Cloudflare Workers, my goal is to create software that is performant, accessible, and maintainable for the long haul.

positions.title: Senior Developer
positions.description:
For over a decade, I was the technical lead for a diverse portfolio of enterprise clients including Marathon Petroleum and Stellar Bank. My primary focus was evolving our internal CMS and deployment workflows from a legacy Windows environment into a modern, high-velocity stack.

- Modernizing the Edge: I migrated a legacy Node.js monolith to Cloudflare Workers. This application previously relied on multiple Linux servers and load balancers. By using native Web APIs like Fetch and Streams, I reduced latency and simplified our global deployment pipeline.
- Developer Experience (DX): I built a custom Node.js local development environment to replace a restrictive classic ASP and IIS setup. This allowed our team to work locally with full environment parity and removed the bottleneck of shared staging servers.
- Component-Based Scaling: To speed up UI development, I built a template engine that transformed regular HTML modules into Gutenberg blocks. This allowed the team to build complex WordPress sites without needing to work in PHP or React for every change.
- Standardizing UI: I introduced Tailwind CSS and a unified project structure across the organization. This shift took our typical UI build time from one week down to a single day.
- Infrastructure Reliability: I managed application-layer configurations across GCP and Rackspace. I maintained 99.9% uptime for high-security clients through automated Git-push workflows and integrated CI/CD testing.

projects.title: San Jacinto Museum of History Redesign
projects.description:
Houston brand experience firm, BrandExtract, LLC, renewed its partnership with the San Jacinto Museum of History to redesign the nonprofit organization’s website, focusing on dynamic, interactive features and increased access to regular and future patrons. Among other goals, the new San Jacinto Museum website is expected to:

• Increase museum attendance
• Increase website visibility and awareness of the Museum among new users
• Help with fundraising efforts

To kick off the project, the entire BrandExtract team visited the monument, museum and Albert and Ethel Herzstein Library.  Located on the 2nd floor of the monument, the lbraryis one of state’s best-kept secrets and a treasure trove for history researchers and geneologists with a Texas hero in their ancestry.

After a research-intensive assessment process, led by Malcolm Wolter  BrandExtract's creative and interactive teams freely explored leading edge tactics and technologies  that were ultimately implemented to create a fully engaging website.

Some key features of the new site include:
• Searchable catalog of the museum's art and artifacts, including photos, descriptions and hundreds of biographical profiles.
• Access to the Herztstein library’s finding aids for both amateur and professional historians..
• Interactive map comparing the battleground in 1836 to the modern landscape
• Engaging, informative illustration of the San Jacinto Monument, built in 1936.
• Detailed timeline recounting the events leading up to the historically critical Battle of San Jacinto
• Battle reenactment videos
• Visitor and educator resources, including the acclaimed Curriculum Guide which has been downloaded and used by thousands of teachers across the Lone Star State
• and much more...

For more information about BrandExtract's process and the website's redesign, read the full case study: LINK

Visit the San Jacinto Museum of History website: http://www.sanjacinto-museum.org
